# DSA In Depth

> Open-source interactive curriculum for data structures, CPU cache hierarchy, and algorithmic invariants, featuring 69 visual step simulators and browser-native C++20/TypeScript coding labs.

- Canonical Site: https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/
- Repository: https://github.com/innovatorved/dsa-in-depth
- License: Code MIT, Written Content CC BY 4.0

## Primary Entry Points

- [Home & Interactive Algorithm Stepper](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/): Overview, live step-by-step algorithm visualizer, simulator previews, and full 6-track curriculum index.
- [Learning Roadmap](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/roadmap/): Dependency DAG across all 6 tracks and 18 modules (180 units).
- [Production Incident Challenges](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/challenges/): Interactive algorithmic debugging scenarios (HashDoS, ReDoS, graph stalls, cache thrashing).
- [Architecture & Capacity Blueprints](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/sandbox/): Interactive topology and algorithmic throughput sandbox.
- [Open-Source Projects & Builds](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/projects/): 22 guided multi-file algorithm builds and engineering case studies.
- [Algorithms Glossary](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/glossary/): Concise asymptotic, structural, and mathematical definitions across 18 modules.
- [Sitemap](https://dsa-in-depth.vedgupta.in/sitemap.xml): Complete list of all pre-rendered URLs.

## Curriculum Tracks (18 Modules · 180 Units)

1. Foundations, Memory Hierarchy & Linear Structures (Modules 1.1–1.3): CPU cache hierarchy, recurrences, amortized potential, arrays, bit manipulation, linked structures, and LRU/LFU.
2. Hashing, Sorting & Divide-and-Conquer (Modules 2.1–2.3): Universal hashing, Robin Hood & SwissTable, sketches, hybrid TimSort/IntroSort, binary search on monotonic spaces, and FFT.
3. Trees, Balanced Hierarchies & Range Queries (Modules 3.1–3.3): BSTs, heaps, AVL/Red-Black/treaps/splay/B+Trees, Fenwick, lazy/persistent segment trees, and Heavy-Light Decomposition.
4. Strings, Automata & Information Retrieval (Modules 4.1–4.2): Radix tries, KMP, Z-algorithm, Aho-Corasick, suffix arrays/automata, FM-index, Thompson NFA, and Myers diff.
5. Graph Theory, Shortest Paths & Network Flow (Modules 5.1–5.3): CSR cache representation, Tarjan SCC & 2-SAT, DSU rollback, Dijkstra/A*/Johnson, Dinic max-flow, and bipartite matching.
6. Dynamic Programming, Combinatorial Search & Advanced Paradigms (Modules 6.1–6.4): Dancing Links, matroids, classical/tree/SOS/digit DP, Convex Hull Trick / Li Chao, WQS binary search, computational geometry, and randomized algorithms.
